title: 1985 AHSME Problem 23
statement: If \[ \begin{aligned} x&=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2},\\ y&=\frac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2}, \end{aligned} \] where \(i^2=-1,\) then which of the following is not correct?

solutions.text:
The numbers are the two nonreal cube roots of unity, so \[ x^n+y^n=2\cos\left(\frac{2\pi n}{3}\right). \] This equals \(-1\) when \(n\) is not divisible by \(3,\) but equals \(2\) when \(n\) is divisible by \(3.\) Of the listed exponents, only \(9\) is divisible by \(3,\) so its displayed equation is the one that is not correct.

Therefore the correct answer is C.
hints: Recognize \(x\) and \(y\) as the two nonreal cube roots of unity
Their powers depend only on the exponent modulo \(3\)
